claims: PCPYLD outputs the low 64 bits from rts low 64 bits and the high 64 bits from rss low 64 bits; the pinned template and runtime macro use that order.
PCPYUD outputs the low 64 bits from rss high 64 bits and the high 64 bits from rts high 64 bits; the pinned intrinsic template uses that order.
PCPYH repeats rt halfword 0 across destination halfwords 0-3 and rt halfword 4 across destination halfwords 4-7.
PEXTLW, PEXTUW, PEXTLH and PEXTLB interleave low or upper source portions with rt in even output positions and rs in odd output positions, matching the pinned unpack intrinsic arguments.
PAND, POR, PNOR and PXOR implement 128-bit bitwise AND, OR, NOT-OR and XOR respectively.
PSUBB and PSUBW perform independent lane-wise subtraction with results truncated modulo 2^8 and 2^32 respectively.
The generated templates use a zero-valued vector when reading register zero and ignore writes to destination register zero; the synthetic probe covers rd==0, source zero, rd==rs and rd==rt.
The actual-template synthetic probe compiled with UBSan and produced zero mismatches for all 13 operations, with 80096 cases per operation.
The synthetic probe establishes full PS2 emulator or game equivalence.

evidence.text: Sony EE Core Instruction Set Manual v6.0, PCPYLD operation: GPR[rd]127..0 ← GPR[rs]63..0 || GPR[rt]63..0; description says high 64 comes from low rs and low 64 from low rt (printed p.190). PCPYUD description: output low/high 64 bits correspond to high rs/high rt respectively (p.191). PCPYH description: repeats each least-significant halfword of each 64-bit half into its four halfwords (p.189). https://docs.alexrp.com/mips/ee_insns.pdf

Sony EE manual: PEXTLW interleaves words from low-order 64-bit portions of rs and rt (p.205); PEXTUW interleaves words from high-order 64-bit portions (p.208); PEXTLH interleaves halfwords from low-order 64-bit portions (p.204); PEXTLB interleaves bytes from low-order 64-bit portions (p.203). Exact PEXTLW output low words: rt0,rs0,rt1,rs1; PEXTUW: rt2,rs2,rt3,rs3. The operation figures and descriptions confirm rt then rs in low-to-high destination lanes. https://docs.alexrp.com/mips/ee_insns.pdf

Sony EE manual PAND computes 128-bit `GPR[rs] AND GPR[rt]` (p.176); PNOR computes `GPR[rs] NOR GPR[rt]` (p.252); POR and PXOR are parallel bitwise OR and exclusive OR (pp.253,285). PSUBB truncates each byte subtraction to 8 bits (p.270); PSUBW truncates each word subtraction to 32 bits (p.284). https://docs.alexrp.com/mips/ee_insns.pdf

Pinned PCSX2 MMI.cpp commit 81526d4dc7cc70e4ae75abb35a789417456c6d43: PCPYLD writes RD.UD[1]=RS.UD[0], then RD.UD[0]=RT.UD[0]; PCPYUD writes RD.UD[0]=RS.UD[1], then RD.UD[1]=RT.UD[1]. PCPYH sets destination halfword lanes 0..3 from RT.US[0] and 4..7 from RT.US[4]. PEXTLW uses RT words 0,1 alternating with RS words 0,1; PEXTUW similarly RT then RS for words 2,3; PEXTLH and PEXTLB use RT then RS alternating over the low halfwords/bytes. PAND/POR/PXOR apply the corresponding bitwise operation; PNOR uses bitwise complement of OR; PSUBB/PSUBW subtract corresponding byte/word lanes. All listed handlers return immediately when rd==0. https://github.com/PCSX2/pcsx2/blob/81526d4dc7cc70e4ae75abb35a789417456c6d43/pcsx2/MMI.cpp

Pinned PS2Recomp c5a9d02573410a2085a4b4b831b0b68ba3515440: runtime `#define GPR_VEC(ctx_ptr, reg_idx) ((reg_idx == 0) ? _mm_setzero_si128() : ctx_ptr->r[reg_idx])`; `SET_GPR_VEC` only assigns when reg_idx!=0. PCPYH template first loads `__m128i src = GPR_VEC(ctx, rt)` before setter. Other tested templates pass source vector values to intrinsics/macros, then setter writes destination.

mmi-packed-audit-03/run.json: actual-template-probe compiled with clang++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=undefined using SSE2NEON; exit 0, stderr empty, 13 operations each checked 80096 cases, mismatches all zero. The C++ wrappers were generated from exact format strings in pinned mmi_translation_helpers.cpp and macro definitions in ps2_runtime_macros.h. Vectors include basis, boundary, and 10000 deterministic random cases; modes distinct registers, rd==rs, rd==rt, rd==0 with sentinel, rs==0, rt==0, both sources zero, and rd==rs==rt. No game routine or emulator executed.
